title: sufr writes to the home directory without being asked
body:
Every place the two crates write a file, outside tests, at 1b1ecd0. The table at 6629ab0 also listed the build's merge scratch file in the system temp directory. 01aa478 removed it, and `NamedTempFile` now appears only in tests.

| site | what | where | asked for? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `libsufr/src/build.rs`, `build` | the `.sufr` output | the path given to `build_to_file` | yes |
| `libsufr/src/typed.rs`, `cache_dir` and `write_cache` | the subsample cache | `~/.sufr/locate-<m>-<basename>`, the directory created if absent | no; never removed |
| `sufr/src/lib.rs`, `create_output` | search output under `-o` | the path given | yes |
| `sufr/src/main.rs` | the log under `--log-file` | the path given | yes |

The cache is the one Jack asked about on 2026-11-03. `typed::open` (`typed.rs`) has `TypedSuffixArray::open` build a subsample when the suffixes are opened in memory and `max_query_len` is shorter than the file's sort length. That length is `Header::sorted_len`: the text length for an unmasked file and the mask weight for a masked one. `subsample_with_cache` writes the subsample to the home directory and reads it back on later runs. Ken added it in ea9415c (2024-11-07). Its problems:

- The key is the file's basename and `m` alone, so two files with one name share a cache entry; the stale check is by mtime only, so an older file with the same name reads the other's subsample.
- Nothing removes an entry. Jack's `~/.sufr` held 43 files from the tests and the sweep.
- `home_dir()` is unwrapped with `expect`, so no home directory is a panic.
- The library writes to the user's home on a read operation, from inside `SuffixArray::open_with`, with no option to decline.
- `read_cache` reads native-endian bytes into a `Vec<W>`. The alignment problem of sufr-bc4784 (closed) was fixed in bd21d2e, and the byte order is the machine's, as in the `.sufr` arrays.

The build's scratch file was the other write nobody asked for. dev's `--tmp-dir` option for it (db9b5a9) was dropped because the build has no scratch file now (sufr-f5785e, closed).

## Proposal

Decide whether the cache is removed, kept next to the `.sufr` file, or written to an explicit directory from the caller with no default outside the output path. The tests then stop depending on the home directory for free. Until decided, the tests that open a file with `-m` and the suffixes in memory run with `HOME` set to a temp dir. These are the `extract` and `locate` helpers and `count_under_a_cap_matches_count_without_one` in `sufr/tests/cli.rs` (7c0f393, sufr-f5ec10), and `open` in `libsufr/tests/search.rs`.

## Open

- Whether the subsample is worth caching at all. It is one linear pass: over the LCP array when the file has one, and otherwise over the suffix array and the text. For the fixtures it is microseconds, and for a genome it is the same read `-l` makes on every query.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: The subsample cache reads and writes T in native byte order through as_bytes and as_bytes_mut in libsufr/src/io.rs, the same convention the .sufr arrays use. Whatever replaces the cache inherits that. Since 7c0f393 the extract and locate helpers in sufr/tests/cli.rs and every test in libsufr/tests/search.rs point HOME at a temp dir, so the suite no longer writes to ~/.sufr.
